daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo predicted Indonesia's economy will surpass Germany, Britain, and France, according to expert forecasts, while separately raising performance allowances for Defence Ministry employees and TNI soldiers. The president also inaugurated 1,204 IPDN graduates as Pamong Praja Muda civil service officers, expressing pride that the top graduates came from farmer and labourer families. Prabowo additionally instructed BMKG to strengthen El Niño anticipation measures.

  • The KPK arrested Pemalang Bupati Anom Widyantoro in a dawn operation related to project acceptance and position-buying, with the bupati's wife also arriving at KPK and the DPUPR office sealed.
  • DPR Commission III deputy chair urged police and KP2MI to take extraordinary measures against human trafficking.
  • The DPR will formulate comprehensive solutions in response to the rising number of regional heads caught in KPK sting operations.
  • A labour coalition delivered draft proposals for a Labour Law to DPR factions during a visit to parliamentary groups.
  • DPR Speaker Puan Maharani called on the government to prioritize water crisis management in facing El Niño conditions.
  • A Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting (SMRC) poll found that Prabowo would lose if elections were held today, while another SMRC survey showed majority skepticism about village cooperatives' future.
  • DPR member Bakri bin Musa passed away, according to official reports.
  • An activist coalition launched a petition calling for a halt to remilitarization, while TNI Commander Dudung stated Komcad is voluntary service, not mandatory military conscription.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia promoted sustainability and resilience in ASEAN disaster management through regional forums. The country also strengthened ties with Morocco through cultural diplomacy initiatives. In defence modernization, digital transformation advanced at I Gusti Ngurah Rai Air Base through the Gatra Akasa program.

  • UK Export Finance announced readiness to deploy £4 billion to support Indonesian infrastructure and energy projects.
  • Indonesia and China held discussions to explore strategic housing cooperation in Jakarta focused on affordable housing development.
  • The Indonesian futsal team scheduled friendly matches with Spain in preparation for the 2028 World Cup qualifiers.

Other

The government tightened refined sugar imports to protect local cane farmers and ordered sugar processors to own local cane plantations. Indonesia's economy is projected to maintain growth above five percent in the second quarter of 2026. The Trade Ministry strengthened small business protection on digital marketplaces through new regulations.

  • Indonesia broke ground on a 40 MW waste-to-energy plant, with West Java separately launching a project for Greater Bandung worth Rp 7.2 trillion.
  • The Health Ministry released investigation findings into the death of an internship doctor who fell from an 18th-floor apartment in South Jakarta, revealing the doctor suffered from mental health issues and had taken medication since medical school, with the ministry reporting six intern doctors died in 2026, mostly from illness.
  • Indonesia secured a US$2.3 billion investment in a coal-to-methanol project, while the country's first electric heavy equipment factory in Karawang aims to reduce infrastructure costs.
  • Indonesian rice field eels entered the Chinese market, while the textile industry faces calls to boost global competitiveness with traditional textiles showing US$251.34 million export potential.
  • The Health Ministry proposed Bogor as a model for integrated tuberculosis control programs nationwide.
